Launched January 5, 2026. H-series Panther Lake SKU: 4P+4E+4LPE (12 total, no Hyper-Threading). TDP: 15-25W base, up to 80W max turbo. Integrated GPU: Intel Xe3 Graphics (4 Xe3 cores).

Launched January 5, 2026. H-series Panther Lake SKU, distinguished from the 336H by a stronger 10-Xe3-core Arc B370 iGPU (vs. the standard 4-core Xe3 graphics on most other Ultra 5/7 H-series parts). 4P+4E+4LPE (12 total, no Hyper-Threading). TDP: 15-25W base, up to 80W max turbo. Integrated GPU: Intel Arc B370 (10 Xe3 cores).
Launched January 2026. Non-H (thin-laptop) Panther Lake SKU: 4P+4LPE (8 total threads, no standard E-cores). TDP: 15-25W base, up to 80W max turbo. Integrated GPU: Intel Xe3 Graphics.

Launched January 5, 2026. H-series Panther Lake SKU: 4P+8E+4LPE (16 total, no Hyper-Threading) — fewer P-cores but more total cores than the previous-gen Arrow Lake-H parts (which had 6P+8E). Notably uses a smaller 4-Xe3-core iGPU rather than the fuller graphics config on some sibling SKUs. TDP: 15-25W base, up to 80W max turbo. Integrated GPU: Intel Xe3 Graphics (4 Xe3 cores).
Launched January 2026. Non-H (thin-laptop) Panther Lake SKU, top of the non-H stack: 4P+4LPE (8 total threads). TDP: 25-55W range per corroborating source. Integrated GPU: Intel Xe3 Graphics.

Launched April 2026, quietly added to Intel's lineup without a formal announcement. Confirmed via live Intel ARK page (verified against this session's actual date of Aug 12, 2026). New top-tier 'Core Ultra X' branding introduced for Panther Lake, sitting alongside — not above — the near-identical Core Ultra X7 368H; per Tom's Hardware/TweakTown reporting, the X9 378H's only functional difference from the X7 368H is that it lacks embedded-segment support, being exclusive to consumer products. A separate, higher-tier Core Ultra X9 388H also exists as the true flagship. Flagship-tier core config: 4P+8E+4LPE (16 total, no Hyper-Threading). TDP: 15W min-assured, 25W base, 80W max turbo. Integrated GPU: Intel Arc B390 (12 Xe3 cores).
